For an owner in the **Caribbean and Latin America** who wants **brand affiliation** but also wants to preserve **hotel individuality**, the brands most commonly considered are **soft-brand or collection-style flags** such as **Autograph Collection**, **Curio Collection by Hilton**, **Tapestry Collection by Hilton**, **Vignette Collection**, **Destination by Hyatt**, **The Luxury Collection**, **Ascend Hotel Collection**, and **Radisson Individuals**.[7][12][14][1]

These brands are especially relevant because they are positioned around **distinctive, independent, or one-of-a-kind hotels** rather than highly standardized full-brand formats. For example, Marriott’s **Autograph Collection** and **The Luxury Collection** are described in the region as supporting authentic, locally inspired, or unique properties, while Hyatt’s **Destination by Hyatt** is explicitly a collection of independent hotels offering one-of-a-kind destination experiences.[7][3][12] Choice’s **Ascend Hotel Collection** and **Radisson Individuals** likewise target hotels with unique characteristics and personalities that still meet the brand’s quality standards.[1][5]

Other brands sometimes considered for a similar reason, depending on the owner’s level of flexibility and segment, include **Vignette Collection** and **Kimpton** under IHG, since IHG describes Vignette as a curation of distinct hand-picked hotels and Kimpton as part of its luxury/lifestyle set in the region.[4][13][9]

If you want, I can narrow this to the **best-fit options by segment** — luxury, upscale, lifestyle, or select-service.
